name: Self-repairing machine
definition: A machine or system that detects its own faults and repairs itself, running unattended for long periods.
doubt: Refused in first pass; check whether a real self-repairing machine milestone exists (e.g. fault-tolerant self-repairing computers, 1970s).

name: Teleoperated robot and telepresence
definition: A robot or manipulator operated remotely by a person who sees, and sometimes feels, through its sensors.

first_pass.what: Raymond Goertz at Argonne National Laboratory built a master-slave manipulator for handling radioactive material (patent filed 1949; some sources say 1948 design; GE's Payne had a similar 1948 device)

first_pass_note: telepresence with feeling later; first priority contested

name: Robotic exploration probe
definition: An uncrewed robot vehicle that explores another planet, the deep sea or space and reports back.

first_pass.what: Soviet Lunokhod 1 rover landed on the Moon (Luna 17) and was driven remotely from Earth for about 11 months (earlier flyby/impact probes not checked)

first_pass_note: deep-sea and other probes not checked

name: Microscopic robot
definition: A robot or machine built at microscopic or molecular scale, for example to work inside the body.

first_pass.what: Nature papers showed DNA-based molecular robots (molecular spiders walking programmed origami tracks; DNA assembly line); autonomous DNA walkers date to 2004. No in-body use yet

name: 3D printing
definition: A machine that builds solid objects automatically from a digital design by adding material layer by layer.

first_pass.what: Chuck Hull filed the stereolithography patent (US 4,575,330, granted 1986-03-11); Kodama filed a similar patent weeks earlier
3D Systems introduced the SLA-1, first commercial stereolithography machine (sources vary 1987 to 1988)

name: 3D scanning of objects
definition: A device that records the complete shape or structure of an object so that it can be reproduced.

first_pass.what: Cyberware Laboratories released its laser-stripe Head Scanner producing 3D computer images of the human head (touch-probe CMMs earlier, unverified)

name: Aircraft and spacecraft autopilot
definition: A control system that flies or steers an aircraft, ship or spacecraft on a set course without a human at the controls.

first_pass.what: Lawrence Sperry flew a Curtiss with gyroscopic autopilot hands-off at the Paris Concours de la Securite en Aeroplane; system developed 1912

first_pass_note: practical use and mass adoption not researched

name: Spacecraft guidance and navigation computer
definition: A computer that calculates orbits, courses and engine burns and steers a spacecraft or ship along them.

first_pass.what: Apollo Guidance Computer, designed by MIT Instrumentation Lab, first flew on Apollo 7 (Oct 1968) and guided Apollo 11 to the Moon in 1969 (Gemini computer 1965 not checked)

name: Self-driving car
definition: A road vehicle that drives itself to a destination without a human driver.

first_pass.what: Ernst Dickmanns' VaMoRs Mercedes van drove itself on an unopened autobahn using cameras and computers (Tsukuba 1977 vehicle was rail- or marker-aided)

first_pass_note: Waymo One 2018 had safety drivers; fully driverless public service not verified, so no practical use given
doubt: 1987 VaMoRs; earlier driverless cars (guided by buried wires, 1950s; Tsukuba 1977) may fit.

name: Drone (unmanned aerial vehicle)
definition: An aircraft without a pilot on board that flies by remote control or by itself to scout, carry or attack.

first_pass.what: Hewitt-Sperry Automatic Airplane flew about 1,000 yards pilotless under gyroscopic control (US Navy test); Kettering Bug tests Sept-Oct 1918

name: Computer-run space station
definition: A computer that runs the life support, systems and operations of a space station or colony.

name: Computer-run government
definition: A state, city or planet whose policy and administration are decided by a central computer rather than by people.

name: Computer forecasting of social behaviour
definition: A computer that predicts elections, markets, wars or individual behaviour by statistical models of people.

first_pass.what: CBS used UNIVAC I on election night to forecast the presidential result; it predicted an Eisenhower landslide (438 EV vs actual 442)

first_pass_note: psychohistory not real; UNIVAC election forecasting is the real analogue

name: Computerized economic planning and finance
definition: Computers that plan production, manage an economy or analyse and trade on financial markets.

first_pass.what: Chile's Project Cybersyn (Stafford Beer, Fernando Flores) sent daily production data from nationalized factories by telex to a central mainframe in Santiago; used by the Allende government, notably in the October 1972 strike

first_pass_note: No milestone given. NYSE DOT (1976) only routed orders and is not trading or analysis; 1980s program trading was not pinned down.

name: Computerized marketing and consumer analytics
definition: Computers that measure audiences, score customers and predict what they will buy.

first_pass.what: Fair, Isaac & Co. introduced its first credit application scoring system for a small finance company in Louisiana. Whether it ran on a computer at the time is not confirmed.

first_pass_note: Credit scoring 1958 used; Nielsen Audimeter (1939-46) is a meter, not a computer, and was left out.
